title: introduce-regression-primer-and-probabilistic-flaky-filter-ci-adapter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Adds a lightweight "regression primer" workflow and a probabilistic flaky-prompt filter CI adapter to the eval-harness. Motivation: CI noise from transient prompt flakiness has been increasing (see ENG-5423) and leads to false-positive regressions; teams need a reproducible primer run and a statistical filter to avoid blocking merges for low-confidence failures. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: (1) regression primer: a fast pre-eval sampler that runs a deterministic, stratified subset of prompt anchors to produce a baseline expectation before full evals are scheduled; (2) probabilistic flaky filter: a small statistical layer that consumes per-prompt pass/fail histories and flags low-confidence failures (based on Bayesian posterior of failure rate) as soft-fails, emitting structured metadata so downstream automation can decide quarantine/retry policy; (3) CI adapter: GitHub Check integration and a CLI flag (--primer-mode) to run primer-only checks and annotate PRs with primer delta summaries. The description below documents config knobs, safety considerations, and operational expectations.

Config and behaviour: primer runs are limited to a configurable budget (default 200 prompts or ~5% of prompt set, whichever is smaller), use stratified sampling over cohorts and prompt difficulty bins, and always use a fixed seed and deterministic environment to maximize reproducibility. The flaky filter maintains an in-repo lightweight ledger (TTL-backed JSON) storing recent per-prompt outcome counts; on each run the filter computes a Beta posterior and a one-sided credible interval for the true failure rate. Failures with posterior probability > 0.9 of exceeding the configured threshold (default 15%) are marked hard-fail, while failures with medium probability (0.5-0.9) are labeled soft-fail and annotated with the posterior and suggested actions (retry, quarantine, human review).

Operational notes: the ledger is bounded (N latest entries per prompt) and the filter can operate in two modes: local-only (no external storage) and central ledger (optional S3/GCS). Latency overhead on CI is < 8% in practice (benchmarked on our smoke CI runners). The adapter emits structured JSON annotations and a human-readable primer delta summary inserted into the PR body. We intentionally keep the primer small so it is cheap to run on every PR; teams can opt into larger primer budgets in repo-level config.

Security and data: no model outputs are stored in the ledger, only pass/fail booleans and prompt identifiers; prompt ids can be hashed in high-security repos. We added config options to disable ledger persistence in private/on-prem installs.

Compatibility: integrates with existing eval-harness CLI and the GH Checks plugin; no change required to eval pipelines for baseline runs. Backwards-compatible default behaviour is unchanged: unless --primer-mode or the flaky filter is enabled in config, runs behave as today.

Related work: ENG-5423 (primer proposal), ENG-5499 (flaky-filter spec). This PR includes unit tests, deterministic smoke runs, and a migration script to generate an initial ledger from historical CI results (optional).
